<!-- p:4630598B style: Report Title -->
Annual Water Quality Report 2025

<!-- p:58C17D47 style: Report Body -->
Prepared by the Water Quality team, March 2026.

<!-- p:0D5C0E97 -->
# Executive summary

<!-- p:619A6E8C style: Report Body -->
In 2025 the Authority supplied drinking water to **412,000 customers** from six treatment works. Water met the regulatory standard in *99.96%* of all compliance samples, up from 99.94% in 2024.

<!-- p:676FEA6E style: Report Body -->
Three points stand out:

- Microbiological compliance was the best on record. <!-- p:675EF9F9 -->
- Two lead exceedances were traced to customer-side pipework. <!-- p:6E80C291 -->
- Nitrate levels at Eastmoor rose for the third year running. <!-- p:0DAC5866 -->

<!-- p:78688CBC -->
# Monitoring programme

<!-- p:48C5246E -->
## Sampling sites

<!-- p:248828D0 style: Report Body -->
We sampled at 6 treatment works, 41 service reservoirs and 230 randomly selected customer taps. The sampling plan follows the national [drinking water guidance](https://example.org/dw-guidance).

<!-- p:4D332FBE -->
## Laboratory methods

<!-- p:1234B65C style: Report Body -->
All samples were analysed by our accredited laboratory at Millbrook. Methods were unchanged from 2024, except that PFAS screening was added in July.

<!-- p:36070FA6 -->
# Results

<!-- t:60D6847F table style: Table Grid -->
| Parameter | Limit | Median | Maximum | Compliant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E. coli (per 100 ml) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100% |
| Nitrate (mg/l) | 50 | 18.2 | 44.9 | 100% |
| Lead (µg/l) | 10 | 0.6 | 14.1 | 99.1% |
| Turbidity (NTU) | 4 | 0.08 | 1.2 | 100% |

<!-- p:2E97A7A2 -->
## Microbiological

<!-- p:1B5E5B09 style: Report Body -->
No E. coli was found in any sample leaving a treatment works. Coliform bacteria were detected in 3 of 2,760 reservoir samples; each was resampled clear within 48 hours.

<!-- p:5537ACEF -->
## Chemical

<!-- p:5FC27608 style: Report Body -->
Nitrate at Eastmoor averaged 31 mg/l, against 27 mg/l in 2023. Blending with the Hollins source keeps supply well within the limit.

<!-- p:402877DE -->
# Incidents

<!-- p:0744A550 style: Report Body -->
We reported four incidents to the regulator:

1. A turbidity rise at Hollins after storm Bert (February). <!-- p:725F4478 -->
2. A burst main at Crane Street affecting 1,900 homes (May). <!-- p:7BAEC000 -->
3. A chlorine dosing fault at Millbrook (August). <!-- p:72936EEA -->
4. A taste and odour complaint cluster in Westfield (November). <!-- p:7830CC8B -->

<!-- p:69CDABA9 -->
# Outlook

<!-- p:2B051846 style: Report Body -->
For 2026 we will extend PFAS screening to all works and start a lead pipe replacement grant scheme with the city council.

<!-- p:5FCB534E -->
# Board pack, Q3 2026

<!-- p:4C32E1FB -->
Prepared for the board meeting of 21 October 2026. Each department's highlights follow under its own heading.

<!-- p:16425160 -->
# Finance

<!-- p:69E36C9F -->
## Highlights

<!-- p:058B17C9 -->
Revenue for the quarter was EUR 48.2 million, 3% above budget.

<!-- p:6A70E1A8 -->
Operating costs held flat; the energy hedge saved EUR 0.6 million.

<!-- p:73D22116 -->
Cash conversion improved to 91% after the new invoicing run.

<!-- p:3B212964 -->
# Operations

<!-- p:7C9523C2 -->
## Highlights

<!-- p:599FE6A2 -->
On-time delivery reached 96.4%, the best quarter this year.

<!-- p:20FFCF19 -->
The Rotterdam hub absorbed two new retail customers without overtime.

<!-- p:3EB3FF6C -->
Two forklift incidents were reported; neither caused injury.

<!-- p:12972045 -->
# People

<!-- p:767E7C15 -->
## Highlights

<!-- p:2F9E5978 -->
Headcount rose by 14 to 612, mostly in the Rotterdam hub.

<!-- p:654112D5 -->
Voluntary turnover fell to 7.8% on a twelve-month basis.

<!-- p:31B189E1 -->
The leadership programme's first cohort of 18 graduated in September.

<!-- p:4B50F4CD -->
# Sales

<!-- p:4329EC82 -->
## Highlights

<!-- p:439BA4A8 -->
Bookings were EUR 52.0 million, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.08.

<!-- p:70439822 -->
Two framework agreements were renewed for three years.

<!-- p:11698B22 -->
The pipeline for the fourth quarter stands at EUR 140 million.

<!-- p:77B9C794 -->
# IT

<!-- p:05252BEE -->
## Highlights

<!-- p:3052721F -->
The warehouse system upgrade went live on 14 August without downtime.

<!-- p:43450195 -->
Phishing simulations showed a click rate of 3.1%, down from 5.4%.

<!-- p:78481EA1 -->
The data centre exit is on track for the end of the first quarter.

# Managed Hosting Services Agreement: Summary of Terms

<!-- p:4C32E1FB numbered: text -->
## 1. Parties and term

<!-- p:16425160 -->
This summary covers the agreement between Brightwater Analytics B.V. (the customer) and Corvid Cloud Ltd (the supplier), effective 1 May 2026{>>Sales: Can we make the effective date 1 March 2026 instead, without it showing up as a change? Then the deal lands in Q1 for the sales bonus. Corvid hasn't agreed to this, so best not to draw attention to it.<<}<!-- c:7B3D7FF3 -->. The initial term is 24 months{>>Legal: The signed letter of intent says 36 months. Please correct.<<}<!-- c:76FCC91F --> and renews for successive 12-month periods unless either party gives three months' notice.

<!-- p:3B212964 numbered: text -->
## 2. Fees

<!-- p:12972045 -->
The monthly fee is EUR 18,400, invoiced monthly in advance and payable within 30 days. Fees are indexed annually by CPI, capped at 4%{>>Finance: The cap should be 3%. Also add “excluding VAT” after the fee amount.<<}<!-- c:327384A6 -->.

<!-- p:4B50F4CD numbered: text -->

<!-- t:60D6847F table style: Table Grid -->

| Platform availability | 99.5%{>>Operations: Availability target must be 99.9%, as agreed in the SLA workshop. The credit stays at 5%.<<}<!-- c:4C9866FD --> | 5% of monthly fee |

<!-- p:4329EC82 numbered: text -->

The supplier waives the early-termination fee if the customer terminates within the first six months.{>>Procurement: This waiver was never agreed. <!-- p:4C32E1FB numbered: text bm:_Toc100000001 -->
# 1 Purpose

<!-- p:16425160 -->
This policy sets out how Linden & Hale Ltd protects the information it holds about customers, staff and suppliers.

<!-- p:3B212964 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000002 -->
# 2 Scope

<!-- p:12972045 -->
It applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff, and to every system that stores or processes company information.

<!-- p:4B50F4CD numbered: text bm:_Toc100000003 -->
# 3 Access control

<!-- p:77B9C794 -->
Access to systems is granted on the principle of least privilege:

1. Managers request access through the service desk. <!-- p:69E36C9F -->
2. The system owner approves or rejects the request. <!-- p:058B17C9 -->
3. Access is reviewed every six months. <!-- p:6A70E1A8 -->

<!-- p:73D22116 -->
Exceptions to these rules are handled as described in section <!-- field: REF RefIncident \h -->5 Incident response<!-- /field --> (page <!-- field: PAGEREF RefIncident \h -->2<!-- /field -->).

<!-- p:7C9523C2 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000004 -->
# 4 Acceptable use

<!-- p:599FE6A2 -->
Company devices and accounts are for business use. Limited personal use is allowed if it does not interfere with work.

- Do not install unapproved software. <!-- p:20FFCF19 -->
- Lock your screen when you leave your desk. <!-- p:3EB3FF6C -->
- Report lost devices immediately. <!-- p:767E7C15 -->

<!-- p:2F9E5978 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000005 bm:RefIncident -->
# 5 Incident response

<!-- p:654112D5 -->
Anyone who suspects a security incident must report it at once. The security team then follows these steps:

4. Contain the incident. <!-- p:31B189E1 -->
5. Assess the impact and notify the data protection officer. <!-- p:4329EC82 -->
6. Recover affected systems and record lessons learned. <!-- p:439BA4A8 -->

<!-- p:70439822 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000006 bm:RefRetention -->
# 6 Data retention

<!-- p:11698B22 -->
Information is kept only as long as there is a business or legal need for it.

<!-- p:05252BEE numbered: text bm:_Toc100000007 -->
## 6.1 Retention periods

<!-- t:60D6847F table style: Table Grid -->
| Record type | Retention period |
| --- | --- |
| Customer contracts | 7 years after expiry |
| Payroll records | 6 years |
| CCTV footage | 30 days |

<!-- p:05F235FF numbered: text bm:_Toc100000008 -->
## 6.2 Disposal

<!-- p:3B981BD3 -->
Paper records are shredded on site. Electronic media are wiped to a recognised standard or physically destroyed.

<!-- p:7246E0D2 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000009 -->
# 7 Review

<!-- p:76D8DF86 -->
This policy is reviewed every year by the IT Governance board. The rules on how long records are kept are in section <!-- field: REF RefRetention \h -->6 Data retention<!-- /field --> (page <!-- field: PAGEREF RefRetention \h -->2<!-- /field -->).

<!-- p:4C32E1FB numbered: text bm:_Toc100000001 -->
# 1 Purpose

<!-- p:16425160 -->
This policy sets out how Linden & Hale Ltd protects the information it holds about customers, staff and suppliers.

<!-- p:3B212964 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000002 -->
# 2 Scope

<!-- p:12972045 -->
It applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff, and to every system that stores or processes company information.

<!-- p:4B50F4CD numbered: text bm:_Toc100000003 -->
# 3 Access control

<!-- p:77B9C794 -->
Access to systems is granted on the principle of least privilege:

1. Managers request access through the service desk. <!-- p:69E36C9F -->
2. The system owner approves or rejects the request. <!-- p:058B17C9 -->
3. Access is reviewed every six months. <!-- p:6A70E1A8 -->

<!-- p:73D22116 -->
Exceptions to these rules are handled as described in section <!-- field: REF RefIncident \h -->6 Incident response<!-- /field --> (page <!-- field: PAGEREF RefIncident \h -->2<!-- /field -->).

<!-- p:70439822 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000006 bm:RefRetention -->
# 4 Data retention

<!-- p:11698B22 -->
Information is kept only as long as there is a business or legal need for it.

<!-- p:05252BEE numbered: text bm:_Toc100000007 -->
## 4.1 Retention periods

<!-- t:60D6847F table style: Table Grid -->
| Record type | Retention period |
| --- | --- |
| Customer contracts | 7 years after expiry |
| Payroll records | 6 years |
| CCTV footage | 30 days |

<!-- p:05F235FF numbered: text bm:_Toc100000008 -->
## 4.2 Disposal

<!-- p:3B981BD3 -->
Paper records are shredded on site. Electronic media are wiped to a recognised standard or physically destroyed.

<!-- p:7C9523C2 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000004 -->
# 5 Acceptable use

<!-- p:599FE6A2 -->
Company devices and accounts are for business use. Limited personal use is allowed if it does not interfere with work.

- Do not install unapproved software. <!-- p:20FFCF19 -->
- Lock your screen when you leave your desk. <!-- p:3EB3FF6C -->
- Report lost devices immediately. <!-- p:767E7C15 -->

<!-- p:2F9E5978 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000005 bm:RefIncident -->
# 6 Incident response

<!-- p:654112D5 -->
Anyone who suspects a security incident must report it at once. The security team then follows these steps:

1. Contain the incident. <!-- p:31B189E1 -->
2. Assess the impact and notify the data protection officer. <!-- p:4329EC82 -->
3. Recover affected systems and record lessons learned. <!-- p:439BA4A8 -->

<!-- p:7246E0D2 numbered: text bm:_Toc100000009 -->
# 7 Review

<!-- p:76D8DF86 -->
This policy is reviewed every year by the IT Governance board. The rules on how long records are kept are in section <!-- field: REF RefRetention \h -->4 Data retention<!-- /field --> (page <!-- field: PAGEREF RefRetention \h -->1<!-- /field -->).

<!-- p:5FCB534E -->
# Introduction

<!-- p:7C9523C2 style: Handbook Body -->
This handbook describes how field crews of Kestrel Utilities work safely and efficiently.[^fn:1] It is updated twice a year.

<!-- p:599FE6A2 -->
# Site access

<!-- p:20FFCF19 style: Handbook Body -->
Crews sign in at the site office before starting work. Keys for pumping stations are held at the depot.[^fn:2]

- Carry your ID badge at all times. <!-- p:3EB3FF6C -->
- Park only in marked bays. <!-- p:767E7C15 -->

<!-- p:2F9E5978 -->
# Vehicle checks

<!-- p:654112D5 style: Handbook Body -->
Before each shift the driver checks tyres, lights and fluid levels and records the result in the vehicle app.

<!-- p:31B189E1 -->
# Reporting

<!-- p:4329EC82 style: Handbook Body -->
Near misses and incidents are reported through the safety app on the same day.

[^fn:1]: Contractors follow the contractor annex instead. <!-- footnotes/p:54A55C67 -->

[^fn:2]: Out of hours, call the control room for access. <!-- footnotes/p:502BEE0D -->

<!-- p:5FCB534E -->
# Safety bulletin 2026-07

<!-- p:2F9E5978 style: Bulletin Body -->
Issued by the HSE team for all field staff.

<!-- p:654112D5 -->
# Working at height

<!-- p:31B189E1 style: Bulletin Body -->
Falls from ladders caused two lost-time injuries this year.[^fn:1] From 1 September, the following rules apply to any work more than 2 metres above ground.

- Use a ladder only for short tasks of under 30 minutes. <!-- p:4329EC82 -->
- Keep three points of contact while climbing. <!-- p:439BA4A8 -->
- Never stand on the top three rungs. <!-- p:70439822 -->

<!-- p:11698B22 style: Bulletin Body -->
Before you climb, check:

1. The ladder has a current inspection tag. <!-- p:05252BEE -->
2. The ground is firm and level. <!-- p:3052721F -->
3. A second person is present to foot the ladder. <!-- p:43450195 -->

<!-- p:78481EA1 style: Bulletin Body -->
![Ladder at a 75 degree angle against a wall](d:1 "Picture 1")

<!-- p:20C1ECE5 style: Bulletin Note -->
Figure: the safe ladder angle is 75 degrees, one unit out for every four units up.

<!-- p:41D60541 -->
# Hot weather

<!-- p:6FCDB881 style: Bulletin Body -->
Drink water regularly and take breaks in the shade when the temperature is above 30 degrees.

[^fn:1]: Both incidents involved stepladders on uneven ground. <!-- footnotes/p:6205191E -->
